subject: general
question: Kelvin and Kin can together finish work in 25 days. They worked together for 15 days and then Kin left. After that, Kelvin finished the remaining work in 12 days. In how many days, can Kelvin alone finish the work?
solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Kelvin and Kin together = 25 days

Kin left after 15 days

Kelvin finished the remaining work in 12 days

**Formula used:**

Work Done = time × efficiency

**Calculation:**

Let kelvin and kin be A and B respectively-

⇒ A + B = 25 Days

⇒ 1 Day Work by A and B = 1/A + 1/B

⇒ 1/A + 1/B = 1/25

According to Question -

⇒ (1/A + 1/B) ×15 + 1/A × 12 = 1

⇒ 1/25 × 15 + 1/A × 12 =1

⇒ 1/A × 12 = 1 - 15/25

⇒ A = large{(25 × 12)/(10)} 

⇒ A = 30 Days

∴ The correct answer is 30.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

According to question,

Time taken by Kelvin and Kin together = 25 days

Kin left after 15 days

Kelvin finished the remaining work in 12 days

So, (Kelvin + kin) × 25 = (Kelvin + Kin) × 15 + Kelvin × 12

⇒ 25 Kelvin + 25 Kin = 27 Kelvin + 15 Kin

⇒ 10 Kin = 2 Kelvin

⇒ Kin/Kelvin = 1/5

Total Work = (Kin + Kelvin) × 25 = 6 × 25 = 150

Time taken by Kelvin alone = 150/5 = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**
